_note: Furniture in furnished accommodation: ten per cent a year of its cost, or the hire charges where hired from a third party, less what the employee pays for it (D-111). TY 2026-27: Income-tax Rules, 2026 r.15(2)(e) (p.1542), "(i) … increased by 10% per annum of the cost of furniture (including television sets, radio sets, refrigerators, other household appliances, air-conditioning plant or equipment), as reduced by any charges paid or payable for the same by the employee during the tax year; and (ii) if such furniture is hired from a third party, the value of perquisite would be the actual hire charges payable for the same as reduced by any charges paid or payable". TY 2025-26: Income-tax Rules, 1962 r.3(1) Table I col. 4 as substituted by G.S.R. 615(E) (pp.4–5), to the same effect. This row is the ten per cent; PerquisiteNode apportions it to the period by days, takes hire charges as entered, and takes off the employee's charges. Every regime. It reaches the providers of Table I Sl. 1 and 2 only (W-158b): TY 2026-27, r.15(2)(e)(i), "the value of perquisite as determined under Table I: Sl. Nos. 1 and 2. C be increased", and Sl. 3, the hotel, is "Not applicable." in column C, its column D the lower of the hotel's charges and 24% of salary; TY 2025-26, Table I column (4) adds the furniture to Sl. (1), (2)(a) and (2)(b), and Sl. (3)'s column (3) is "Not applicable", its column (4) the hotel's value alone (sources/2026-10-24-accommodation-furniture.md F1, F2).
